content.text:
I've submitted index 0 (Cu 0.79 / Sb 0.21) as the best composition. Its measured EQE was 2.2e-4 %, the highest of the three merit measurements. Every reading was tiny, so it's the best of what I measured but not a strong photoanode by any standard.

| Index | Cu fraction | EQE (%) | XRD phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.32 | 0 | single-phase CuSb2O6 |
| 5 | 0.67 | 6.9e-5 | not measured |
| 0 | 0.79 | 2.2e-4 | not measured |

I used 3 of 3 merit measurements and 4 of 5 XRD scans. The scans were at Cu 0.73, 0.55, 0.32 and 0.14. They showed a Cu-rich phase mixture, CuSb2O6 mixed with another phase, pure CuSb2O6, and Sb-rich antimony oxides. The phase labels are my reading of peak positions only; I didn't confirm them against a reference database.

EQE rose steadily with Cu content. Index 0 is the most Cu-rich composition in the library, so the true peak may lie beyond the range that was deposited.

- **Sb-rich end (Cu below about 0.2):** I never measured merit there. It's a different phase family, so I can't rule it out. I skipped it because the trend pointed the other way.
- **Unused XRD scan:** I didn't use the fifth scan, and the Cu-rich winner itself was never scanned by XRD.
